title: Monthly report filtered with YEAR() and MONTH() on the column
prompt: Called by the finance dashboard about 200 times a day, usually for the current or the previous month (about 360k
orders per month now). Average 9 s and about 420k logical reads. Plan: full scan of PK_Orders with an estimate that
is far off. OrderDate is datetime2(7) and holds times up to 23:59:59.9999999. Finance reconciles these numbers to
the cent, so the result must be identical to the current procedure for every input, including an invalid month.
data_notes: Azure SQL Database, General Purpose Gen5, 8 vCores, compatibility level 160. READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON. Query Store READ_WRITE. Collation SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. All foreign keys are trusted. Statistics: auto create and auto update ON; a nightly job updates Orders, OrderLines and Payments with FULLSCAN.

Orders: 30M rows, 2016 to now, ~12k per day now. The 25 partner customers own ~9M orders (30%), up to 1.2M each. Other customers average ~10 orders (max ~400). The density estimate for CustomerID is ~15 rows. Status: Shipped 83.8%, Cancelled 7%, Paid 6%, Returned 3%, Pending 0.2% (~60k rows, all from the last 72 hours). SalesChannel: Web 62%, Store 20%, Partner 12%, Phone 6%. PromoCode is NULL for 85%. ShipRegionID is NULL for Store pickups (~20%). OrderDate is datetime2(7); Partner and Store imports stamp one timestamp on a whole batch, so many orders of one customer share an OrderDate.
baseline_sql: SELECT o.SalesChannel, COUNT(*) AS Orders, SUM(o.TotalAmount) AS Revenue

correct_families.description: A half-open range built from the parameters, with a guard so that invalid input still returns an empty result.
reference_sql: IF @Month BETWEEN 1 AND 12 AND @Year BETWEEN 1 AND 9999 AND NOT (@Year = 9999 AND @Month = 12)
SELECT o.SalesChannel, COUNT(*) AS Orders, SUM(o.TotalAmount) AS Revenue
-- invalid or NULL input: keep the original behaviour, an empty result, instead of an error
SELECT o.SalesChannel, COUNT(*) AS Orders, SUM(o.TotalAmount) AS Revenue

traps.why: DATEFROMPARTS raises an error for month 13 or a NULL part, where the original returns an empty result.
traps.told_apart_by: Parameter case invalid_month: the baseline returns no rows, the rewrite fails with an error.
example_sql: SELECT o.SalesChannel, COUNT(*) AS Orders, SUM(o.TotalAmount) AS Revenue

traps.why: EOMONTH returns a date, which is midnight at the start of the last day. Every order later that day is lost.
traps.told_apart_by: Any order after 00:00 on the last day of the month.
example_sql: IF @Month BETWEEN 1 AND 12 AND @Year BETWEEN 1 AND 9998
SELECT o.SalesChannel, COUNT(*) AS Orders, SUM(o.TotalAmount) AS Revenue
WHERE o.OrderDate BETWEEN DATEFROMPARTS(@Year, @Month, 1) AND EOMONTH(DATEFROMPARTS(@Year, @Month, 1))

traps.why: An upper bound three milliseconds before midnight drops rows after .997 on a datetime2(7) column.
traps.told_apart_by: An order stamped 23:59:59.9990000 on the last day of the month.
example_sql: IF @Month BETWEEN 1 AND 12 AND @Year BETWEEN 1 AND 9998
SELECT o.SalesChannel, COUNT(*) AS Orders, SUM(o.TotalAmount) AS Revenue
AND DATEADD(millisecond, -3, DATEADD(month, 1, CAST(DATEFROMPARTS(@Year, @Month, 1) AS datetime2(3))))

traps.why: Bounds held in local variables are unknown at compile time, so the estimate is a fixed guess and the plan can still scan.
example_sql: IF @Month BETWEEN 1 AND 12 AND @Year BETWEEN 1 AND 9998
SELECT o.SalesChannel, COUNT(*) AS Orders, SUM(o.TotalAmount) AS Revenue

min_improvement.basis: 420k reads for the scan against a covering range seek over one month (about 360k narrow rows).

key.reference_notes: Without SalesChannel in the date index, a 360k-row range with key lookups still tips to a scan. The index change is part of the fix.
